newsitem.title: USA: NFL-HOBBLED YOUNG LEADS 49ERS TO VICTORY ON COMEBACK SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: NFL-HOBBLED YOUNG LEADS 49ERS TO VICTORY ON COMEBACK SUNDAY.

text.p: Steve Young, hobbled by a strained groin muscle, rolled left and ran 15 yards for a touchdown with 68 seconds left as the San Francisco 49ers rallied from down 21-0 to beat the Cincinnati Bengals 28-21.
Young, who missed San Francisco's last three games due to the groin injury, had hit rookie Terrell Owens with a 45-yard touchdown pass with 2:08 left to tie the game at 21-21.

Young aggravated the injury when he was sacked in the second quarter and was replaced by Elvis Grbac with the Niners trailing 14-0. But Grbac hurt his left shoulder late in the second quarter, forcing Young to return.
"I don't think they (the coaching staff) were planning on doing that, but I told them I could hobble on in there," said Young. "I'm glad I got the chance to go back in."
Young played the entire second half and directed three touchdown drives for a win that kept the 49ers (5-2) tied with the Carolina Panthers for first-place in the NFC West.
The Benglas dropped to 1-6.
At Denver, John Elway threw for 329 yards and three touchdowns, all to Ed McCaffrey, as the Broncos rallied for 14 fourth-quarter points to beat the Baltimore Ravens 45-34.
Elway clinched victory with a nine-yard dash for a score with 1:16 to play. Baltimore fell to 2-5.
AFC West leaders Denver (6-1) trailed 34-31 when Elway directed a 10-play, 57-yard march for the go-ahead score.

In Houston, Willie Davis and rookie Eddie George scored fourth-quarter touchdowns less than two minutes apart as the Houston Oilers moved into a first-place tie in the AFC Central Division with a 23-13 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The Oilers (5-2) gained a measure of revenge for a 30-16 setback at Pittsburgh (5-2) three weeks ago. In that game, the Oilers were beaten and beat up as there were three separate brawls that led to 35 players being fined a total $145,000.
In Dallas, Troy Aikman hooked up with Kelvin Martin on a 60-yard touchdown pass with 1:42 remaining to lift the Dallas Cowboys to a 32-28 victory over the winless Atlanta Falcons.

It was the third straight win but another lackluster effort for Dallas (4-3), who look nothing like the defending Super Bowl champions as the season nears its midway point. The team squandered a 17-6 lead, missed dozens of tackles and had to rally against the worst pass defence in the NFL.
Michael Irvin, playing his second game since his five-game suspension, returned to form with seven catches for 119 yards.
In Washington, the Redskins opened up a 28-point lead and survived a New York comeback to post a 31-21 victory.
Terry Allen rushed for three TDs and Darrell Green ran back an interception 68 yards for a score as Washington (6-1) maintained a one-game lead over Philadelphia in the NFC East.
New York (2-5) trailed 28-0 at the half but battled back to 28-21 before Washington's late field goal iced it.
In Philadelphia, Ty Detmer threw four TD passes to former Dolphin Irving Fryar and Ricky Watters scored on a 49-yard run with 2:28 left as the Eagles downed Miami 35-28.
Detmer, making his second career start in place of the injured Rodney Peete, completed 18-of-24 passes for 224 yards.
"We had a great game plan coming in, we had a lot of time up front," said Detmer, as the Eagles soared to 5-2.
"He likes me and I like him," said Fryar about adjusting to Detmer as quarterback.
Watters ran for 173 yards against Miami (4-3).
At Carolina, John Kasay kicked four field goals and Kerry Collins tossed a 13-yard touchdown pass to Mark Carrier as the Panthers beat the New Orleans Saints 19-7.
The second-year Panthers (5-2) totalled 21 first downs and 314 yards total offence while holding New Orleans (2-6) to just 10 first downs and 174 yards. Carolina remained tied for the NFC West lead.
In Indianapolis, Curtis Martin rushed for two third-quarter touchdowns to lead the New England Patriots to a 27-9 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.
The win improved the Patriots to 4-3 and moved them within one game of Indianapolis (5-2) and Buffalo in the AFC East.
Indianapolis quarterback Jim Harbaugh suffered a broken nose after being sacked by defensive end Willie McGinest midway through the fourth quarter and did not return.
"It was a right cross to the face," said Harbaugh. "The first guy yanked my face mask, and the second guy got me on a right cross. I'll be back next week."
At New York, Steve Christie's team-record sixth field goal of the game, a 47-yarder with 10 seconds remaining, gave the Buffalo Bills a 25-22 victory over the winless New York Jets.
Quarterback Jim Kelly struggled again for Buffalo (5-2), but directed a nine-play, 51-yard drive to the winning kick.
The Jets (0-8) had rallied to tie the game on ex-Bill Frank Reich's 21-yard scoring strike to Wayne Chrebet.
In St Louis, Tony Banks scrambled 22 yards to set up the go-ahead score and Jacksonville failed to get off a potential game-tying field goal in the final seconds as the Rams edged the Jaguars 17-14.

Trailing 14-10 early in the fourth quarter, the Rams (2-5) moved 86 yards in nine plays for the go-ahead score. The Jaguars (3-5) drove inside the St Louis 10 but were not able to stop the clock before the gun sounded.
At Arizona, Kent Graham tossed a five-yard touchdown pass to Larry Centres and Greg Davis kicked two field goals as the Arizona Cardinals defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 13-9.
Arizona improved to 3-4, while Tampa Bay dropped to 1-6.
